newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia starts $2.5 bln urban transport project.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia starts $2.5 bln urban transport project.

text.p: A conglomerate controlled by Indonesian President Suharto's daughter set up a joint venture with two state-owned companies on Monday to construct a 6.06 trillion rupiah ($2.5 billion) elevated rail and road line in Jakarta.

PT Citra Lamtoro Gung Persada, owned by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana, joined state-owned toll-road operator PT Jasa Marga and railway company Permuka to set up PT Citra Moda Margakencana Persada, which will build the project.
"God willing, this project will help ease traffic jams in this beloved city," Rukmana said in a speech at a ceremony marking the setting up of the new company.
The elevated, three-tier thoroughfare, which will connect southern and downtown Jakarta, will consist of a 23.65-km (14.78-mile) toll road, a 22 km (13.75 mile) railway line and a public road.
Construction would start in December and the project is to be completed in 2001. Funding will come from a consortium of domestic and foreign banks.
Further details have not been announced.
